The Nigeria Police has confirmed that 30 Niger State residents were killed in the reprisal attack that followed the killing of village head, Mallam Bawa Muhammed. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, made this known in a statement in Niger State on Wednesday after an on-the-spot visit to Wawa and Gada Oli communities in Borgu Local Government Area, led by the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada. Iniedu confirmed that a reprisal attack following bandit attacks on Lumma Ba’are and Wawa communities in Borgu resulted in the deaths of 30 people, not 64 as reported in the media. “DIG Nadada, CP Fago, senior officers, and the Borgu Local Government Chairman proceeded to Lumma Ba’are and Wawa communities for on-the-spot assessments and stakeholders’ engagements over the 21st November 2026 attacks, which claimed six lives and left several houses burnt in Lumma Ba’are before a suspected reprisal later that day resulted in the loss of over 30 lives in Wawa,” he said. Iniedu said the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, deployed DIG Nadada to Niger State to conduct an on-the-spot assessment of the bandit attack and the reprisal killings in the Fulani community in the LGA, following allegations that Fulanis led the bandits to the community where the village head was killed alongside five other people in Borgu. He warned that communal violence and reprisal attacks only worsen insecurity, assuring the Emirate Council that additional operational assets and tactical teams would be deployed to stabilise the area. “Following the palace visit, DIG Nadada, CP Fago, senior officers, and the Borgu Local Government Chairman proceeded to Lumma Ba’are and Wawa communities for on-the-spot assessments and stakeholders’ engagements over the 21st November 2026 attacks, which claimed six lives and left several houses burnt in Lumma Ba’are before a suspected reprisal later that day. “DIG Nadada announced the deployment of additional tactical personnel to reinforce joint security teams already operating in the area, while reminding residents that sustaining peace is a collective responsibility requiring active community cooperation,” Iniedu said.
